plan.summary: This 1-4 block is an off-camp boxing build with one weekly S&C session, so the plan keeps the highest-value work: power first, then main strength, then practical accessories, then short conditioning. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main percentage-based lift, and the main training starts in Week 2. Because your boxing load matters more than gym volume, this block uses low exercise count, clear technique, and steady progression you can recover from.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body power, foundational strength, and work capacity with simple high-value lifts.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress strength and power with slightly heavier work while keeping fatigue controlled around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength topped up and express faster, sharper power with lower fatigue.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height that lets you land quietly and stable every rep. Step down between reps and stay explosive.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if boxes are limited. Reset between reps and jump for height with a clean landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want the simplest jump option. Start from a still position and keep reps crisp.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Warm up in small jumps, then work up to one hard set of 3-5 reps with clean form. Stop at the heaviest set you can complete without hitching or losing position. This sets your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your training max.

substitutionOptions.name: Block Pull
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if trap bar setup is unavailable. Pull from just below the knee with the same hard but clean top set.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Use a load you can control with a full pause at the top for each rep. Keep the chest glued to the pad.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no chest-supported row is available. Keep the torso still and finish with the elbows.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if machines are busy. Brace well and avoid twisting.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Only roll out as far as you can while keeping ribs down and lower back flat. Move slowly and stay braced.

substitutionOptions.name: Stability Ball Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the ab wheel is too difficult. Keep the same braced trunk position.

substitutionOptions.name: Cable Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need a simpler trunk option. Move the spine with control and avoid yanking the rope.

exercises.name: Air Bike Intervals
exercises.notes: Push hard but keep the first round under control so the quality stays high.

endurancePrescription.format: 8 rounds of 15 seconds hard, 45 seconds easy
endurancePrescription.intensity: Hard on work bouts, easy spin on recovery

substitutionOptions.name: Row Erg Intervals
substitutionOptions.notes: Use the same work-rest format. Drive hard with the legs and relax on recovery.

substitutionOptions.name: Sled Push Intervals
substitutionOptions.notes: Use 8 rounds of 15 seconds fast push, 45 seconds walk back and recover. Keep the load light enough to move quickly.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no box is available. Reset between reps and jump for height.

substitutionOptions.name: Trap Bar Jump

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Drive hard from the floor, keep the chest tall, and finish with full hip extension. Rest enough to keep every set clean.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track bar speed, load, and rep quality on all work sets. If all sets feel sharp and clean, add a small jump next week.
